label: GitHub Copilot CLI

skills.note: Copilot CLI's own location. It would also read .claude/skills, but DDW does not make one tool depend on another tool's directory.

hooks_note: The scripts land in the repo; the manifest that points at them does NOT. GitHub's hooks reference says policy hooks are available 'regardless of folder trust state' — the others are not. Repository hooks load only in a folder the user has trusted, and trust is answered in a dialog `copilot -p` cannot show. Measured 2026-08-22/23 with trustedFolders as the only variable: trusted, 3 hooks ran and the write was refused; not trusted, 0 ran and the file was written; user-level, refused either way. The trap is that trust is invisible — the repo a developer has used interactively is trusted and enforces, the same repo on CI is not and does not. install.sh writes ~/.copilot/hooks/ddw.json instead, once per machine, pointing at each repo's scripts by relative path. Not both levels: where the folder is trusted the reference says every source is combined and all run, so two levels judge every write twice.

choice_prompt.note: the ask_user tool — agent and Plan mode; absent in Ask mode
